# fluid

Generated by fluid-design from `fluid.config.json`. Nothing in this folder is
hand-edited: change the config and run `fluid generate`, or change a setting
(below) with no regenerate at all.

## Install

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import './fluid/fluid.css';
```

That one import brings the units, the settings, the base layer, the breakpoints,
the band variants and every `fluid-*` utility.

Browser zoom needs one script in `<head>`, before first paint:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { FluidHead } from '@/styles/fluid/integrations/next'
<html><head><FluidHead /></head>…
```

## Tuning: settings are CSS variables

Every number you tune is a CSS variable with a registered default. Set the
ones you want to change in your own `:root`, next to your tokens:

```css
:root {
  --fluid-phone-scale-min: 0.8;
  --fluid-desktop-display-damping: 0.7;
}
```

`settings.reference.css` lists every one with its default and what it does.
Order does not matter, an invalid value falls back to the default, and
changes apply live. `fluid check` lints them, `fluid explain 390x844` shows
what everything resolves to at a viewport and where each value came from.

## Bands

- **phone** — phone — portrait phones, the 390 artboard. `(width < 600px) and (not ((orientation: landscape) and (height <= 500px)))`
- **tablet** — tablet — 600px and wider: the phone design, scaled up. `(600px <= width < 1024px) and (not ((orientation: landscape) and (height <= 500px)))`
- **landscape** — landscape — a phone on its side (500px tall or less): the phone design, scaled a bit. `(width < 1024px) and (orientation: landscape) and (height <= 500px)`
- **desktop** — desktop — 1024px and wider: the 1440×900 artboard. `(width >= 1024px)`

Authors write each drawing once: the phone numbers for every mobile band,
the desktop numbers from `lg:` up. Only the unit changes between bands.

## Units

| Unit | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `--fluid` | layout: spacing, sizes, positions (`fluid-p-*`, `fluid-w-*`, …) |
| `--fluid-display` | display type (`fluid-display-64/72`): damped, so it shrinks less than the layout |
| `--fluid-copy` | copy type (`fluid-copy-64/72`): damped, so it shrinks less than the layout |
| `--fluid-text` (via `fluid-text-*`) | type inside a box that scales with the layout |
| `--fluid-ui` | the header, nav, footer: follows the width, never shrinks for a short window (`fluid-ui-h-*`, …) |
| `--fluid-container-width` / `-padding` | the page container (`fluid-container`) |
| `--header-h` | the header's height, safe area included |

Scripts read the same units as numbers: `fluidPx(600)`, `fluidPx(24, 'copy')` (from `fluid.ts`).

## Why it is built this way

- **One scale per band, no per-section re-anchoring.** A section drawn taller
  than the artboard is more than one screen at every viewport.
- **min() of the two desktop axes** (fit, not cover): a section drawn as tall
  as the artboard never outgrows the window. svh, not dvh, so type does not
  resize mid-scroll when a mobile toolbar collapses.
- **Damped type**: a heading shares its column with fixed measures, so it
  rides a gentler curve than the layout. Below the desktop band's edge the
  damping is read at the edge (the "knee"), which is what holds headings up
  on a short window.
- **×1000 precision**: every comparison runs on lengths scaled by 1000 and
  divides once, because Firefox rounds a min()/max() result to 1/60 px.
- **Unitless numbers**: `calc(64 * var(--fluid))`, never `64px * var(--fluid)`
  (length × length is invalid and the browser drops it silently).
- **Not scaled on purpose**: border widths, `tracking-*` (use em), fixed text
  measures.
